title: Environmental DNA Sampling Protocols for Marine Non-Indigenous Species Surveillance
author: Luca Mirimin

Prior to deployment, each net and other reusable equipment must be decontaminated in order to remove any DNA trace form previous use. While most materials and small equipment can be easily decontaminated by soaking in 20% bleach for at least 20 minutes (with occasional mixing/turning), it is recommended that nets must be fully submerged in bleach in a large deep tray and rinsed with DNA-free water at least 3 times while rubbing and "massaging" the net and seams by hand to remove any excess bleach.

"Site name/code", "Date", "Rep n" It is recommended to secure the label by covering it with a strip of sellotape to avoid risk of mislabeling.

steps.title: Establish risk assessment
steps.instruction: Conduct a thorough risk assessment to minimize risk of harm to users and other parties before beginning any sampling activity.

steps.title: Plan sampling and record metadata
steps.instruction: Decide sampling platform (boat, floating or fixed structure) based on survey goal; for each sample/location record date, time, GPS/location, replicate number, other code, operator name, and environmental parameters.

steps.title: Don clean single‑use gloves
steps.instruction: Put on clean, single‑use gloves; change gloves immediately if they contact clothing, skin, or non‑DNA‑free equipment; for easy changes wear double gloves and replace only the outer glove.

steps.title: Pre‑label Whirl‑Pak bags
steps.instruction: For each site, pre‑label the required number of Whirl‑Pak bags with “Site name/code”, “Date”, and one of: “LV Water field blank”, “Rep 1”, “Rep 2”, … “Rep n”.

steps.title: Prepare field blank water control
steps.instruction: Fill the pre‑labelled field‑blank Whirl‑Pak bag with DNA‑free water at the site; keep the bag upright in a cool, dark place (e.g., black bin bag or cooler box) until filtration.

steps.title: Collect water samples
steps.instruction: Fill each remaining pre‑labelled Whirl‑Pak bag (e.g., Rep 1) with site water either from the surface using a DNA‑free pole and bag adapter or at depth using a DNA‑free Niskin bottle (rinse the Niskin three times with site water before collection). Take at least one extra sample beyond the intended number to compensate for possible loss. Seal bags properly, keep them upright, store them in a cool, dark place during transport and before filtration, and record all metadata (Site name/code, GPS, Date, Rep #, time of deployment, etc.) for each sample.

steps.title: Record water‑parameter data (optional)
steps.instruction: If a water‑parameter meter is available, measure and record temperature, salinity, depth, pH, dissolved oxygen, etc., together with the other metadata.

steps.title: Decontaminate reusable gear between sites
steps.instruction: Before moving to a new location, wipe the Whirl‑Pak pole, clamps, and adapters with 20 % bleach solution and let them sit for at least 15 minutes. Prepare several pre‑sterilized sets of clamps and adapters (ideally one set per intended site) to reduce cross‑contamination and sampling time.

steps.title: Set up filtration workstation
steps.instruction: In the field or DNA‑free laboratory, put on clean single‑use gloves, wipe the work surface with 20 % bleach, and, if in the field, spread a disposable or reusable plastic sheet (tarpaulin). Assemble the filter pump, power source (mains, battery, or car), and multi‑filter manifold if available; ensure all connections are tight and water/air flow is directed away from the filters. The peristaltic pump may be replaced with a manual pump or a drill‑connected pump head.

steps.title: Pre‑label 15 mL falcon tubes
steps.instruction: Label 15 mL falcon tubes (pre‑filled with 4 mL silica beads) using the same scheme as for the Whirl‑Pak bags; cover each label with a strip of sellotape to prevent mis‑labeling.

steps.title: Filter water samples and store filters
steps.instruction: Place DNA‑free adapter‑funnel‑filter assemblies into the tubing or manifold, keeping the funnel vertical and secure. For each sample, filter the water gradually, swirling the Whirl‑Pak bag to pour suspended particles into the funnel. Using DNA‑free forceps, remove the top membrane filter (not the lower support pad), fold it into a semi‑circle, and place it into its corresponding pre‑labelled falcon tube. Store tubes in a cool, dark place for short‑term storage and transfer them to –20 °C as soon as possible for medium‑ to long‑term storage. Record the time of filtration for each sample.

steps.title: Deploy and retrieve in‑situ sampler
steps.instruction: Select a deployment site with at least 2 m water depth at low tide and clear of boat traffic. After the filtration cycle completes (e.g., 25 hours), retrieve the sampler, remove the filter capsule, and expel excess water through the outflow using a pump, large syringe, or gravity with DNA‑free equipment. Fill the capsule with fixative, optionally inject 1 mL internal positive control (IPC), and seal both ends with caps and/or Parafilm. Label the sample and keep it in a cool, dark place until extraction.

steps.title: Process field negative filter capsule
steps.instruction: If a field negative is required, fill a filter capsule on site with fixative and optional IPC, then store or process it together with the other samples.

steps.title: Pre‑label 50 mL falcon tubes for net samples
steps.instruction: For each site, pre‑label the needed 50 mL falcon tubes with “Site name/code”, “Date”, and one of: “Net field blank”, “Rep 1”, “Rep 2”, … “Rep n”; cover each label with sellotape.

steps.title: Collect net field blank
steps.instruction: Using a 100 % ethanol squeeze bottle, rinse the pre‑decontaminated net and collect 40–50 mL ethanol‑filled liquid into the falcon tube labelled “Net field blank”.

steps.title: Tow net and process plankton samples
steps.instruction: For each replicate, tow the net for the planned distance or time (e.g., 50 m transect) keeping it fully submerged. Before retrieval, concentrate material into the dolphin bucket by several vertical dips, then remove excess water by angling the net so water drains through the bucket mesh; if draining is slow, close off a portion of the net above the bucket to increase surface area. While the net is held high, rinse the bottom of the net with ethanol from the squeeze bottle into the dolphin bucket, detach the bucket, rinse its screens, and transfer the material into a 50 mL falcon tube (splitting into additional tubes if needed). Ensure the final ethanol concentration is at least 80 % in each tube.

steps.title: Store plankton samples on ice
steps.instruction: Place the collected plankton samples out of direct sunlight, preferably on ice and in a rack, keeping them upright to avoid leakage and contamination.

steps.title: Pre‑label sediment tubes and field blank
steps.instruction: For each site, pre‑label falcon tubes for sediment samples and a “Sediment field blank” using the same labeling scheme; cover labels with sellotape.

steps.title: Rinse box corer and collect field blank
steps.instruction: Using a 100 % ethanol squeeze bottle, rinse the inside of the decontaminated box corer and collect 40–50 mL ethanol‑filled liquid into a falcon tube labelled “Sediment field blank”. Store this blank out of direct sunlight, preferably on ice and in a rack, keeping it upright.

steps.title: Deploy box corer and collect sediment
steps.instruction: Deploy and retrieve the box corer; allow seawater on top of the sediment to drain, then use a falcon tube to scoop approximately 10 mL of sediment from the top 1–2 cm layer.

steps.title: Rinse sediment and repeat replicates
steps.instruction: Rinse the corer with site water, redeploy, and repeat the collection steps until the desired number of replicate sediment samples has been obtained.

steps.title: Add silica beads to sediment tubes
steps.instruction: Fill each sediment falcon tube with 30 mL silica beads on top of the sediment (or more if the sediment exceeds 10 mL, maintaining a 3:1 bead‑to‑sediment ratio). Store tubes in a cool, dark place for short‑term storage and transfer them to –20 °C as soon as possible for medium‑ to long‑term storage. Record metadata (Site name/code, GPS, Date, Rep #, time of deployment, etc.).

steps.title: Handle silica beads safely
steps.instruction: Perform all silica‑bead handling in a ventilated outdoor area or under a fume hood; avoid touching or inhaling the beads.
